items.text: {Despite} the delays, the launch was a success.
items.hint: A one-word preposition of contrast, followed by a noun.

items.text: The report, {which} was published last week, has caused quite a stir.
items.hint: Relative pronoun in a non-defining clause (no 'that').

items.text: {Had} we known about the problem, we would have acted sooner.
She is not {nearly|quite|half} as experienced as her predecessor.
{No} sooner had the meeting started than the fire alarm went off.
It's {worth} checking the figures again before we send them.
We'll go ahead with the launch {unless} the client objects.
{Whatever} you decide, let me know by Friday.
There is {little|no} point in waiting any longer.
He apologised {for} not having replied sooner.
{As} far as I'm concerned, the deal is off.
The more you practise, {the} more natural it becomes.
{So} successful was the campaign that we doubled the budget.
items.hint: Inversion with an adjective: ___ + adjective + was …

items.text: The contract is due {to} expire at the end of the year.
On no account {should|must} the door be left unlocked.
We've hired three new people, two {of} whom speak German.
The project was a success, {albeit} a costly one.
{Not} until the audit did we realise how serious the problem was.
There's no {such} thing as a free lunch.
{Given|Considering} the circumstances, I think we handled it well.
She speaks as {though|if} she owned the company.
The delay was {due|owing} to a shortage of parts.
It was {such} a good offer that we couldn't refuse.
{Were} the price to rise further, we would lose customers.
I've no objection to the plan, {provided|providing} that it stays within budget.
{Much} as I admire her work, I can't support her promotion.
Hardly {had} I sat down when the phone rang.
The figures just don't add {up}.
{What} matters most is that the client is happy.
It was the logistics team {that|who} spotted the error.
We need to cut costs, {otherwise} we'll miss our targets.
Regardless {of} what they say, the decision is final.
By the time the client arrives, we will {have} finished the presentation.
Little {did} they know that the deal was already off.
